sources.content: The first commercial polyphase system was the Redlands, CA Powerhouse. Built by General Electric and pioneered by Elihu Thomson and William Stanley, this was the first 3-phase system. It began operation in 1893, generating 250 kW at 50 Hz, and transmitted over 11 km. sources.content: The document describes the first polyphase system for AC power distribution, which was a two-phase system. It discusses how two-phase power was initially used at places like the 1893 World's Fair due to being easier to understand than three-phase power. Two-phase power was also initially used at Niagara Falls before being converted to three-phase for transmission. However, three-phase power eventually became the standard due to being more efficient and providing constant power flow to motors.

### WorkerResearchOutput

**Title:** Single-Circuit Self-Starting Motor Architectures
**Objective:** Examine the design principles, electrical characteristics, and operational mechanics of single-circuit self-starting motor architectures.

---

### 1. Overview & Operational Mechanics

While a basic single-winding, single-phase induction motor produces a purely pulsating magnetic field—resulting in equal and opposite counter-rotating torque components (as explained by the *double-field revolving theory*) and thus zero net starting torque—certain single-circuit or single-phase-fed architectures achieve self-starting capability without requiring an external multi-phase supply. 

A prominent example of a single-circuit, single-source self-starting architecture is the **shaded-pole motor**. 
* **Design Principles:** The shaded-pole motor utilizes a salient-pole stator structure where each pole is divided into two sections: an unshaded main portion and a shaded portion surrounded by a heavy, short-circuited copper ring or loop (known as a *shading coil*).
* **Flux Phase Displacement:** When an alternating single-phase voltage is applied to the single main winding, the time-varying main magnetic flux ($\Phi_m$) passes through the pole core. A fraction of this flux cuts the short-circuited copper shading ring, inducing a circulating current via transformer action. By Lenz's law, this induced current creates a secondary counter-flux ($\Phi_k$) that lags behind the main flux in time phase. 
* **Asymmetric Rotating Field:** Consequently, the magnetic flux in the shaded portion of the pole reaches its maximum value later than the flux in the unshaded portion. This spatial displacement and temporal phase difference creates an elliptical or sweeping component of magnetic field movement traveling from the unshaded zone toward the shaded zone:
  > *"After synthesis with $\Phi_m'$, it will be $\Phi_s$ in the shaded pole section... so that $\Phi_m$ and $\Phi_s$ with different time phases are pulsed at different sections between the main pole and the shaded pole, to form an elliptical magnetic field and generate a starting torque."* (Source: *KELI Motor Tech / Shaded Pole Architecture*)

---

### 2. Electrical Characteristics & Performance

Because shaded-pole and related single-circuit self-starting motors rely on induced shading currents rather than an independent auxiliary circuit with phase-shifting capacitors, their electrical and mechanical performance metrics possess distinct traits:

* **Low Starting Torque:** Because the temporal phase angle shift between the shaded and unshaded pole sections is inherently small (typically much less than $90^\circ$), the resultant revolving field is weak and asymmetric. 
  > *"Since the phase angle between the shaded and unshaded sections is small, shaded-pole motors produce only a small starting torque relative to torque at full speed."* (Source: *Wikipedia: Shaded-pole motor*)
  Starting torque typically ranges from **40% to 50% of full-load torque**.
* **Low Efficiency & Power Factor:** The continuous current circulating through the low-resistance copper shading ring results in significant $I^2R$ copper losses. Combined with high slip and magnetic leakage, these architectures exhibit low operating efficiency and a poor power factor.
* **Simplified Robust Construction:** Due to the absence of centrifugal switches, complex auxiliary windings, or external capacitors, these single-circuit devices are exceptionally reliable, inexpensive, and mechanically rugged.

---

### 3. Application Domain

Because of their limited starting torque and low efficiency, single-circuit self-starting architectures (such as shaded-pole variants and unexcited single-phase synchronous/reluctance designs) are almost exclusively restricted to low-power, fractional-horsepower applications where continuous reliability and low manufacturing cost outweigh energy efficiency. Typical use cases include cooling fans, small blowers, domestic appliances, and timing mechanisms.

sources.content:
Title: (DOC) Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting
First page of “Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting”. # Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting. A three-phase induction motor will continue to operate when a disturbance of some sort causes the source voltages of the motor to become unbalanced. When an induction motor is operated at unbalanced voltage supply the performance characteristics like efficiency, power factor, input power, output power and losses are affected. The single-phasing occurs when one phase fails as a result of a fuse blowing, protective device opening on one phase of the motor, open phase on one terminal of the motor or other causes. In the single phase induction motors, backward mmf causes torque and speed pulsations. This paper presents a new method to eliminate the instantaneous backward mmf to improve the performance of the single phase induction motor. In the proposed method a calculated reference current which is in quadrature with main winding current instantaneously, is injected to the auxiliary winding. Basic system operation and theoretical analysis are discussed and simulation results in comparison with conventional method which uses sinusoidal voltage supply are presented to validate performance of the proposed method. The paper presents a two-dimensional field-circuit model of a two-winding, single-phase induction machine operating as single-phase, self-excited induction generator. Terminal voltage and currents in stator windings as a function of rotor speed and capacitances of capacitors for resistive loads are also presented. Two Types of Induction Motors Single phase induction motor: The single-phase induction motor is not self-starting. When the motor is connected to a single-phase power supply, the main winding carries an alternating current. In this paper, a single-phase motor is fed from a single-phase power source and again from a two-phase power source, so that the auxiliary coils are not separated after 75% of the motor's speed and have a continuous role in the motor's operation. The purpose of the paper is the investigation of possibility of utilization of a single-phase induction machine, designed and normally operating as a single-phase capacitor induction motor, as a self-excited single-phase induction generator, which can be used to generate electrical energy from non-conventional energy sources.

Title: (DOC) Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting
First page of “Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting”. # Why Single Phase Induction Motor is not Self Starting. A three-phase induction motor will continue to operate when a disturbance of some sort causes the source voltages of the motor to become unbalanced. When an induction motor is operated at unbalanced voltage supply the performance characteristics like efficiency, power factor, input power, output power and losses are affected. The single-phasing occurs when one phase fails as a result of a fuse blowing, protective device opening on one phase of the motor, open phase on one terminal of the motor or other causes. In the single phase induction motors, backward mmf causes torque and speed pulsations. This paper presents a new method to eliminate the instantaneous backward mmf to improve the performance of the single phase induction motor. In the proposed method a calculated reference current which is in quadrature with main winding current instantaneously, is injected to the auxiliary winding. Basic system operation and theoretical analysis are discussed and simulation results in comparison with conventional method which uses sinusoidal voltage supply are presented to validate performance of the proposed method. The paper presents a two-dimensional field-circuit model of a two-winding, single-phase induction machine operating as single-phase, self-excited induction generator. Terminal voltage and currents in stator windings as a function of rotor speed and capacitances of capacitors for resistive loads are also presented. Two Types of Induction Motors Single phase induction motor: The single-phase induction motor is not self-starting. When the motor is connected to a single-phase power supply, the main winding carries an alternating current. In this paper, a single-phase motor is fed from a single-phase power source and again from a two-phase power source, so that the auxiliary coils are not separated after 75% of the motor's speed and have a continuous role in the motor's operation. The purpose of the paper is the investigation of possibility of utilization of a single-phase induction machine, designed and normally operating as a single-phase capacitor induction motor, as a self-excited single-phase induction generator, which can be used to generate electrical energy from non-conventional energy sources.

The plant demonstrated advantages of three-phase, 60 hertz long-distance transmission, which became standard, and promoted nationwide development of affordable hydropower.

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Polyphase alternating current systems, pioneered by Nikola Tesla and developed through notable milestones such as the 1891 Lauffen-to-Frankfurt transmission and the 1893 World Columbian Exposition, revolutionized electrical generation, transmission, and motor utilization [web_fef9fdf046c3, web_b9435cdc9e93]. While multi-phase supplies readily provide the rotating magnetic fields necessary for self-starting motors [web_976cf6443afe], specialized single-circuit architectures—such as the shaded-pole motor—achieve self-starting capability from a single-phase source without external auxiliary circuits [web_db41d76d96d8].

claims.text: Polyphase alternating current systems, pioneered by Nikola Tesla and developed through milestones like the 1891 Lauffen-to-Frankfurt transmission and the 1893 World Columbian Exposition, revolutionized electrical generation, transmission, and motor utilization.
Specialized single-circuit architectures such as the shaded-pole motor achieve self-starting capability from a single-phase source without external auxiliary circuits.

sections.title: Evolution of Polyphase Systems
sections.content: In February 1882, Nikola Tesla discovered the rotating magnetic field, utilizing it to construct the AC induction motor and polyphase system for power generation, transmission, and distribution [web_1556782f964c]. Tesla introduced these concepts in his 1888 paper, 'A New System of Alternating Current Motors and Transformers,' which caught the attention of George Westinghouse [web_1556782f964c]. Polyphase power systems were also independently invented by Galileo Ferraris, Michał Doliwo-Dobrovolski, Jonas Wenström, John Hopkinson, and Nikola Tesla in the late 1880s [web_b9435cdc9e93]. A major milestone in long-distance power transmission was the 1891 Lauffen-to-Frankfurt demonstration, which successfully transmitted polyphase power over 175 km [web_b9435cdc9e93]. Furthermore, the Westinghouse polyphase exhibit at the 1893 World Columbian Exhibition in Chicago showcased the practical utility of polyphase alternating current [web_fef9fdf046c3, web_015c8b86a5c9].

sections.title: Single-Circuit Self-Standing Motor Architectures
sections.content: While basic single-phase induction motors produce a purely pulsating magnetic field with zero net starting torque, shaded-pole motors achieve self-starting capability via a single-circuit configuration. Each pole is divided into an unshaded main portion and a shaded portion surrounded by a short-circuited copper ring or shading coil. The shading coil induces a secondary counter-flux that lags the main flux in time phase, forming an elliptical magnetic field that generates starting torque. Because the phase angle shift is small, shaded-pole motors produce low starting torque—typically 40% to 50% of full-load torque—along with low efficiency and a poor power factor due to continuous copper losses in the shading ring.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.content: The evolution of polyphase systems established highly efficient multi-phase distribution networks that naturally facilitate rotating magnetic fields and motor self-starting [web_976cf6443afe]. Simultaneously, single-circuit architectures such as the shaded-pole motor provide economical, rugged, and self-starting alternatives for fractional-horsepower applications despite inherent limitations in efficiency and starting torque [web_db41d76d96d8, web_65c0c108b1c8].

claims.text: Polyphase systems established multi-phase networks facilitating rotating magnetic fields, while single-circuit shaded-pole architectures provide economical self-starting alternatives for low-power applications despite efficiency limitations.
